title: Aruna Ramchandra Shanbaug v. Union of India

content.caseIdentity: Aruna Ramchandra Shanbaug v. Union of India, (2011) 4 SCC 454
content.facts: The petition concerned Aruna Ramchandra Shanbaug, a nurse left in a persistent vegetative state after an assault, and sought withdrawal of life-sustaining treatment.
questionsBeforeCourt: Whether passive euthanasia and withdrawal of life-sustaining treatment could be permitted in the circumstances.
Who could seek withdrawal of life support for a person in a persistent vegetative state and what safeguards should govern such a decision.
content.ratioDecidendi: The Supreme Court distinguished active and passive euthanasia and permitted withdrawal of life-sustaining treatment in appropriate cases subject to judicial safeguards, including the role of the High Court and an expert medical board, while Parliament had not enacted legislation governing the field.
content.holding: The Court declined the specific request to withdraw Aruna's feeding because of the petitioner's lack of locus, but laid down a legal framework for passive euthanasia and withdrawal of life support in appropriate cases.
content.relevance: Foundational Supreme Court authority on passive euthanasia, persistent vegetative state, patient autonomy, dignity and withdrawal of life-sustaining treatment; later constitutional jurisprudence built on these guidelines.
